title: There Are More Trees on Earth Than Stars in Our Galaxy

scenes.text: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
Scientists counted them using satellites and ground surveys from fifty countries.
The answer? About three trillion trees.
Our galaxy has somewhere between one hundred and four hundred billion stars.
That means roughly ten trees for every single star in the Milky Way.
But we cut down about fifteen billion of them every year. Look up, then look around.

description:
A 2015 study in Nature counted about 3 trillion trees on Earth. The Milky Way has an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars.
That's roughly ten trees per star, and we lose about 15 billion trees a year.
Did you expect that number?
